desc:
The string s is a piece of arithmetic text made of digits, lowercase letters, the symbols + - * / and the parentheses ( and ). Its parentheses are guaranteed to be well-formed: every '(' is closed by a later ')' and they never cross.

The nesting depth of s is the largest number of parentheses pairs that are open at the same moment while reading s from left to right. For example, "(1+(2*3)+((8)/4))+1" has depth 3, reached inside ((8). A string without parentheses has depth 0.

Return the nesting depth of s.
constraints: s contains only digits, lowercase letters, + - * /, ( and )
The parentheses of s are well-formed
hints: Whenever you see '(' you go one level deeper, and whenever you see ')' you come back up one level.
You do not need to store the brackets themselves. A single number, the current depth, tells you everything.
Increase a counter on '(', decrease it on ')', and remember the largest value the counter ever reached. Ignore every other character.
editorial: A stack of open brackets would work, but only its size matters here, so the stack can be replaced by a counter. Scan the string once: on '(' increment the counter and update the best value seen so far, on ')' decrement it, and skip all other characters.

Because the parentheses are well-formed, the counter never becomes negative and ends at 0. The maximum value of the counter over the scan is exactly the largest number of simultaneously open pairs. Time is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
